## Step 3: Checking Bin Quality with CheckM

After MetaBAT2 grouped the assembled DNA into 71 bins, I extracted `contig_112` from the Flye assembly and added it as a separate bin. This was done to check whether an unbinned DNA sequence contained useful genomic information that MetaBAT2 had excluded, bringing the total to 72 bins. I then used CheckM to assess genome completeness and contamination by examining marker genes. Completeness estimates how much of the expected genome is present, while contamination indicates possible mixing of DNA from different organisms. My CheckM run did not produce a final results file, so I used the workshop's prepared results for the next stage. In these results, `contig_328` had 97.62% completeness and 1.64% contamination, while `metabat.26` had 97.56% completeness and 0.67% contamination. Both appear to be good candidates for further analysis.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}

cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

# Extract an additional contig from the assembly
samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_112 > ../metabat/bins_bbd/metabat.72.fa

# Copy bins into CheckM input folder
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/

# Confirm number of bins
ls bins_bbd/*.fa | wc -l

# Submit CheckM analysis
sbatch run_checkm_bbd.sh

# Check SLURM job status
squeue -u $USER

# Inspect CheckM log
tail -n 30 ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm/out/checkm.log

# Copy results into project
cp /pvol/data/mg/bbd/checkm/checkm_results_bbd.txt ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm/

# Inspect CheckM results
head -n 5 ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm/checkm_results_bbd.txt
```

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Checkm shell script contains main analysis command
checkm lineage_wf bins_bbd out -t 6 -x fa -f checkm_results_bbd.txt
```

## Step 5: Selecting Bins Based on CheckM Results
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm

# Examine CheckM results
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt

# Select bins with greater than 15% completeness
awk '$13>15 {print $1}' checkm_results_bbd.txt > bbd_topbins.txt

# Check selected bins
wc -l bbd_topbins.txt
head bbd_topbins.txt
```

After reveiwing the completeness of the 72 bins using checkM, I selected bins with over 15% completeness for further analysis. The completeness estimates how much of a microorganisms genome was recovered during assembly and binning. I used awk to filter completeness values in column 13 and save the corresponding bin IDs to bbd_topbins.txt. This produced 14 bins to be used for further analysis - contig_328 and metabat .26 had the highest completeness estimates. The next step will be to identify which microorganisms these bins may belong tp. However, some bins remain incomplete but may still contain useful information about the Black Band Disease microbial community.
